html:
Javanese Surinamese are the descendants of contract workers brought from Java, in the Dutch East Indies, to Suriname between 1890 and 1939. About 33,000 came.

They were recruited by the Dutch to work on sugar and other plantations after the end of slavery, alongside the Indian workers. Many stayed after their contracts ended and became smallholders, keeping the Javanese language, gamelan music and wayang puppet theatre. Most are Muslims, and some pray facing west, as they did in Java.

They make up about a seventh of Suriname's people and have their own parties. A group returned to Indonesia in 1954. Their story joins Suriname to Java and to the wider movement of Asian labour across the colonial world.
sum: Javanese Surinamese are the descendants of contract workers brought from Java, in the Dutch East Indies, to Suriname between 1890 and 1939. About 33,000 came.
